name: Santo di Teufel
description: Baron Hanzo's cruel son and heir -- a sadistic young fire-mage and demonology dabbler, carrying a stolen ritual knife marked with the sigil of Asmodeus.
narrative:
Santo di Teufel is Baron Hanzo's cruel, entitled heir, trained in his
father's dark arts and trusted with none of them. A junior fire-mage with a taste
for cruelty (Lust 80, Arrogance & Entitlement 75), he is charming and predatory in
equal measure (Seduction 81, Deceit 66).

He arrives in Purewater with the column, and with a barbed ritual knife bearing the
sigil of Asmodeus that his father does not know he has taken. He means to work a
demonic spirit-binding of his own and present it as proof that the blood runs true
in him -- and he is nowhere near skilled enough to do it safely.

**GM:** his agenda is *Bind a demon, and be his father's son*. Left alone he will
choose a victim who cannot fight back, botch the ritual, and flee leaving the knife
behind -- the evidence that ties the di Teufels to the possession scheme. Everything
after that depends on who was in the house.

**What he can actually do (rules).** Almost nothing. Santo taught himself by *tracing* out of a
locked case: he has **Open the Channel** and **Spirit Sight** and that is the whole of his binding
capability. He cannot **Seat the Bound**. He has no **Anchor** and no **Draw Forth** and cannot
**Speak with the Bound** -- he has never once heard the voice of the thing he was trying to move.

He had exactly **one scroll**, lifted from his father's case, and it was a single use of Seat the
Bound. That is why he carried five twists of hair and only ever had one seating: he could cut a
channel into as many women as he liked and finish precisely one of them.

He spent it on Emmeralda and botched the roll, and a scroll is consumed whatever the result. After
that he was a young man with four subjects, a barbed knife, and no means whatsoever -- which is why
he went hunting a *fresh* subject rather than returning to the one already prepared, and why he did
not understand what he had left behind in that room.

**His father does not know the scroll is gone.**

equipment.name: Rapier
equipment.notes: Impale (damage not filled on sheet; CFI standard used)

equipment.name: Ritual knife (soul-knife, symbol of Asmodeus)
equipment.notes: Demonologist's binding knife, stolen from his father's effects. He carries it on his belt. If a binding goes wrong he is likely to leave it behind -- it is the key evidence tying the di Teufels to the possession scheme.

equipment.name: Scroll of Seat the Bound (SPENT)
equipment.notes: Stolen from the third shelf of his father's study, behind the border rolls, out of a case that locks and that Hanzo has never once thought to check. One use. Spent on Emmeralda at the Sylph's Embrace and wasted -- a scroll is consumed on use whatever the result. Still legible, still in the Baron's own hand, and therefore evidence linking Hanzo di Teufel personally to demonology.

extras.class_note: Junior arcane fire-mage / demonology dabbler, Rank 1; far weaker than his father Hanzo. Defining skills: Lore (Demonology) 50, 8 arcane spells (fire-focused).
extras.role: Baron Hanzo's cruel heir; sadistic predator; attempted Emmeralda's spirit-binding ritual (dropped the ritual knife = key evidence).
extras.magic_theme: Fire and lightning (Flaming Hands, Affect Normal Fires, Fireball, Lightning Bolt, Shocking Touch) + utility (Magic Missile, Levitate, Web).
extras.family: Son and heir of Baron Hanzo di Teufel; half-brother/double of the twins Randall & Conall (all three uncannily identical, all Hanzo's sons)
extras.sheet_cleanup_note: On the Roll20 sheet Arcane Casting & Arcane Knowledge were a broken -75 -- supplied working values (Casting 55, Knowledge 50) for a junior mage; GM adjust as desired. Rapier damage was blank on the sheet (CFI standard 1d8 used).
extras.source: Roll20 Classic Fantasy character sheet (And then the Dragons Came campaign)
